news.title: Fake virus popups are flooding screens — Microsoft will never put a phone number in a warning
news.excerpt: Scammers blast loud fake "virus detected" popups with a phone number — close the browser tab or hold the power button 15 seconds to force a restart. Microsoft, Apple, and Google never include phone numbers in real warnings. Source: FTC.gov, Microsoft Support — November 2026.

news.title: Fake CAPTCHAs Tell You to Press Windows+R — Don't Do It
news.excerpt:
Scammers have built 186 fake AI websites that look like legitimate chatbot and image-generator tools. When you visit them, a pop-up appears that looks like a "verify you're human" check. It tells you to press Windows+R, paste a command, and hit Enter. Doing that runs harmful code on your computer.

Real verification checks never ask you to open the Run box or paste commands. If a website tells you to press Windows+R, type something, or run a command — close the tab immediately. Do not follow any keyboard instructions from a webpage.

The fake sites mimic popular AI tools like ChatGPT, Midjourney, and Claude. Always go directly to the official website (openai.com, midjourney.com, anthropic.com) instead of clicking search results.

news.title: Router Security Alert: Thousands of Devices Compromised — Check Yours Now
news.excerpt:
Thousands of routers and network switches have been hijacked in recent weeks. 
Attackers are exploiting known flaws in Zyxel GS1900 switches and SonicWall 
VPN devices — nearly 1,000 Zyxel switches compromised worldwide, and SonicWall's 
SSL-VPN authentication bypass is being actively abused. CISA added six actively 
exploited vulnerabilities to its must-patch list on November 10, including 
flaws in Cisco BroadWorks and Barracuda email gateways.

What to do: Log into your router or switch admin page (usually 192.168.1.1 or 
192.168.0.1 in your web browser). Check for a firmware update and install it 
immediately. If your device is older than 5 years and no updates are available, 
replace it. Change the default admin password if you haven't already.

Why it matters: A compromised router...

news.title: Open Enrollment Scams Are Here — Don't Click That Link
news.excerpt: Open enrollment season runs through January 15, 2027, and scammers are flooding inboxes and phones with fake health insurance offers. The FCC warns that robocalls and texts pretending to be from "Medicare," "your insurance provider," or "Healthcare.gov" spike during this window. They pressure you to "verify" your Social Security number or pay a fee to keep coverage. Real insurers and government agencies never ask for payment or personal info over an unsolicited call or text. What to do: Hang up. Delete the text. If you need to check your coverage, go directly to Healthcare.gov or call the number on your insurance card. Never use a number or link from the message. Source: FCC.gov — November 1, 2026

news.title: Fake Free Software Downloads Hide Password-Stealing Malware — Microsoft Warns
news.excerpt: That "Free" Download Is a Trap. You search for a cracked version of a paid program, a free game, or a tool to activate Windows. The first result promises exactly what you want. You download it, run the installer, and click through. Behind the scenes, that installer silently adds unwanted programs — some route your traffic through your computer, others enroll you in distributed computing, and some steal browser passwords. Microsoft warned Nov 3: a campaign uses trojanized installers to deliver monetization payloads. What to do: Never download "cracked" software, activators, or free versions of paid programs. Get software only from the official website or Microsoft Store. If you ran a suspicious installer, run a full scan with Windows Security (built in, free) and change browser passwords.

news.title: Big Security Updates Today — Microsoft, Google & Apple Released Patches
news.excerpt:
BIG UPDATE DAY: Microsoft, Google, and Apple released important security updates TODAY to protect your computer from real threats.

Microsoft just released patches for Windows and Office — these fix problems that could let hackers cause trouble. Google added a new scam protection to Chrome. Apple fixed issues on iPhone and Mac.

What to do: Turn on automatic updates and let them run overnight. You don't have to do anything special. Most updates install while you sleep.

Why it matters: Hackers target computers that haven't been updated. Updates close the doors they try to open.

posts.summary: Scammers blast loud fake "virus detected" popups with a phone number — close the browser tab or hold the power button 15 seconds to force a restart. Microsoft, Apple, and Google never include phone numbers in real warnings. Source: FTC.gov, Microsoft Support — November 2026.
posts.truth: We'll never sell you software you don't need. If a popup scares you, bring the computer in — we'll check it free and tell you the truth.

posts.title: One USB stick for every ISO — Ventoy boots them all free without reformatting
posts.summary: Ventoy is free at ventoy.net — install it on a USB drive, copy as many ISO files as you want (Windows, Linux, rescue disks), and boot into a clean menu to pick which one to run. No reformatting between ISOs.
posts.truth: Most techs still carry a drawer of single-use USB sticks. One Ventoy drive replaces all of them — I keep Windows 11, Windows 10, Ubuntu, and a dozen rescue ISOs on one 64 GB stick.

posts.title: Windows has a free remote help tool built in — Quick Assist connects you safely
posts.summary: Quick Assist is built into Windows 11 — press Start, type Quick Assist, and open it to get a 6-digit code for someone you trust to help you remotely. No download, no account, no third-party tool.
posts.truth: People pay for TeamViewer or AnyDesk subscriptions when Windows already has a secure, Microsoft-signed remote tool. I use Quick Assist to help customers 20 miles away — it just works.

posts.title: Free portable tool stops Windows tracking cold — O&O ShutUp10++ puts every privacy switch in one window
posts.summary: O&O ShutUp10++ is free at oo-software.com — download the portable version, run it, and click "Apply recommended settings" to block Windows telemetry, data collection, and advertising IDs in one click.
posts.truth: Windows has dozens of privacy settings scattered across menus. This tool gathers them all, explains what each one does, and lets you undo anything. I run it on every computer that comes through the shop.

posts.title: Stop struggling with the Snipping Tool — ShareX is the free screenshot and screen recorder that does it all
posts.summary: ShareX is free at getsharex.com or the Microsoft Store — install it, press Print Screen, and capture any region, window, scrolling page, or screen recording with annotations, arrows, and text in seconds.
posts.truth: The built-in Snipping Tool is fine for one quick crop. But when a customer needs to show me a scrolling error message, record a glitch, or annotate a screenshot for support — ShareX does it all without the hassle.

posts.title: Stop paying for Microsoft Office — LibreOffice is the free alternative that opens every file
posts.summary: LibreOffice is free at libreoffice.org — download the installer for Windows, Mac, or Linux and it opens Word, Excel, and PowerPoint files without a subscription, no account, and no forced AI features.
posts.truth: Most people only use 10% of Office features but pay $100/year for the privilege. LibreOffice handles every document I throw at it — resumes, budgets, presentations — and the files save back to Office formats perfectly.

posts.title: Chrome 157 Emergency Update Fixes Actively Exploited Zero-Day — Update at chrome://settings/help
posts.summary: Google released Chrome the latest version on November 9 fixing nine security issues including an actively exploited zero-day (the vulnerability-2026-125350) in the XML component. Update manually: open Chrome's Settings → Help → About Google Chrome, let it check and download, then click Relaunch.
posts.truth: Most people never close Chrome, so the update sits waiting for weeks. Customers get hit by threats Chrome already fixed. Close the browser tonight. It takes 30 seconds.

posts.title: CISA Adds Six Actively Exploited Vulnerabilities — Update Chrome, Outlook, and Barracuda Now
posts.summary: CISA added six exploited vulnerabilities on November 10 affecting Google Chrome (CVE-2026-125350), Microsoft Outlook (CVE-2026-124194), Barracuda Email Security Gateway (CVE-2026-111560, CVE-2026-116606), Cisco BroadWorks (CVE-2026-20320), and Openwave Webtop (CVE-2026-111793). Update Chrome at `chrome://settings/help`, Outlook via Windows Update, and Barracuda appliances per vendor guidance.

posts.title: Firefox 160 Stable Released with Mailto Blocking, PiP Speed Controls, and MKV Support — Free at firefox.com
posts.summary: Firefox 160 stable was released on November 10, 2026, adding the ability to block websites from repeatedly asking to handle mailto: email links, playback speed controls (0.25x to 2.0x) in the Picture-in-Picture video player, support for Matroska (MKV) files with FLAC, MP3, or PCM audio, and a Mini Window feature for keeping tabs always on top. Update free at firefox.com or through Firefox's built-in updater.
posts.truth: Most people don't realize their browser is the first line of defense. Firefox keeps adding privacy features that actually matter — blocking sites from hijacking your email links is a perfect example. Chrome still lets sites spam that prompt.

posts.title: Microsoft November Patch Tuesday Fixes 1,235 Flaws Including Actively Exploited Outlook Zero-Day
posts.summary: Microsoft's November Patch Tuesday addresses 1,235 security vulnerabilities, including one actively exploited zero-day in Outlook that steals login credentials when a malicious file is opened. The update also includes fixes for Windows, Office, and Edge. Update now via Settings > Windows Update.
posts.truth: Browser and OS exploits are the number one way malware gets in. The Outlook zero-day means just opening a malicious file can steal credentials — no click needed. This is why automatic updates matter: you don't want to be the one who opened that file before patching.

posts.title: Windows 11 November Update Adds Cloud Rebuild Recovery and Redesigned Right-Click Menus
posts.summary: Windows 11 November update adds Cloud Rebuild recovery, redesigned right-click menus, and fixes for Remote Desktop and printing. Rollout is gradual — check Settings > Windows Update to see if it's available for your device.
posts.truth: Cloud Rebuild is a big deal — it lets you reinstall Windows from the cloud without a USB stick, keeping your files. The right-click menu finally gets the classic options back without the extra "Show more options" click. Worth checking for.

posts.title: Clearwave Fiber Expands Lake City Network — Thousands Now Eligible for All-Fiber Internet at clearwavefiber.com
posts.summary: Clearwave Fiber continues expanding its all-fiber network in Lake City, with several thousand residents now able to receive fiber internet service. Check availability at clearwavefiber.com. Fiber offers symmetrical speeds up to 5 Gbps with no data caps.
posts.truth: Fiber is the only internet that doesn't slow down when the neighborhood gets home. Cable and DSL share bandwidth — fiber doesn't. If it's at your address, switch. You'll feel the difference on every video call and download.

posts.title: **Headline:** Windows 11 October Update KB5127648 Breaks Wi-Fi and VPN — Here's the Temporary Fix
posts.summary: If your Wi-Fi or VPN stopped authenticating after the October 13 update (KB5127648), this NTLMv1 restriction may be the cause. Windows Group Policy can restore access. Onyx technicians can check and resolve this for you — call (386) 755-7772 for help.
posts.truth: After Patch Tuesday, Microsoft's default NTLMv1 restrictions can break corporate Wi-Fi and VPN authentication on business networks. The network gear — not the computer — is usually the problem.

posts.title: Test Suspicious Files Safely in Windows Sandbox — Free Disposable PC Built Into Windows 11 Pro
posts.summary: Windows Sandbox gives you a lightweight disposable Windows environment to test untrusted apps, open suspicious email attachments, or visit questionable websites without risking your main system. It resets to a clean state every time you close it. Enable it in Windows 11 Pro/Enterprise via Settings > Apps > Optional features > More Windows features > Windows Sandbox, or run 'OptionalFeatures' and check the box.
posts.truth: People click things they shouldn't. A sandbox lets them click safely. I've had customers open "invoice.pdf.exe" in the sandbox — malware runs, sandbox closes, main system stays clean. It's the closest thing to a "delete button" for bad decisions.

posts.title: Restart Once a Week to Clear Memory Leaks and Stuck Updates
posts.summary: Hold your power button for 15 seconds until the screen goes black, wait a moment, then turn it back on. This clears memory leaks, stuck updates, and sluggish performance. Do it every Friday and your computer will stay snappy.
posts.truth: I see computers that haven't been restarted in weeks — they're slow, updates are stuck, and memory is full of leaks. A full power-cycle (hold 15 seconds) clears it all. Do it Friday, start fresh Monday.

posts.title: Microsoft Released Security Updates for Windows and Office Today — Here's What Changed for You
posts.summary: Microsoft released its monthly security updates for Windows 11, Windows 10, Office, and Edge today. These updates fix problems that could let hackers cause trouble. Let the update run overnight and restart when asked.
posts.truth: Updates are your computer's seatbelt. Skipping them leaves you unprotected.
